findings.title: JWT decoded without verifying the signature
findings.description: decode() only base64-parses the payload. Any team can mint an admin token without knowing the signing key.
findings.exploit: Craft a token with an elevated claim and replay it.
findings.remediation: Call verify() with the algorithm pinned explicitly.

findings.title: Hardcoded JWT signing secret in the repository
findings.description: A literal signing secret is embedded in the code, so it is identical for every deployment and readable by anyone with the source.
findings.exploit: Sign arbitrary tokens offline with the leaked secret. Every token forged this way passes verification, including admin claims.
findings.breaker: None. Checkers present genuine tokens, so scoring is unaffected while teams mint valid identities for any user.
findings.remediation: Load the secret from the environment, rotate it, and reject tokens signed with anything but the current secret.

findings.title: Privilege flag copied straight out of an unverified token
findings.description: An administrative flag is taken from the request's own token payload. Combined with a decode-only token check this is a full account takeover primitive: no secret is needed, only the ability to base64 a claim.
findings.exploit: Take any valid token, edit the isAdmin/role claim, re-base64 the payload and replay the request with the forged token.
findings.breaker: None. The checker uses tokens minted by the service, so it keeps working while teams escalate freely.
findings.remediation: Verify the signature and read privileges from the server-side user record, never from client-supplied token contents.

findings.title: SQL statement built by string formatting or concatenation
findings.description: The statement is assembled from runtime values instead of bound parameters, so a team can read or rewrite any row.
findings.exploit: Boolean, UNION or time based injection in the interpolated value.
findings.breaker: One malformed request from any participant can raise a fatal driver error and the instance stops scoring (IV.5).
findings.remediation: Use parameterised queries exclusively; never interpolate.

findings.title: Optional authentication: the permission flag defaults to permissive
findings.description: The handler starts with the permissive value and only upgrades to the restrictive one when a valid token happens to be present. A request without any credential therefore proceeds down the privileged path instead of being rejected.
findings.exploit: Send the request with no Authorization header. The flag stays at its default and the response is still produced.
findings.breaker: Usually none: checkers authenticate properly, so the permissive default only affects teams.
findings.remediation: Fail closed: return 401/403 unless the credential validated, and compute the permission once instead of defaulting it.

findings.title: Registration-time uniqueness constraint on a per-round value
findings.description: If a checker-visible unique field collides between rounds (fixed login, fixed email, fixed slug) the second round cannot register.
findings.breaker: YES. Round N+1 registration fails outright.
findings.remediation: Make the checker's random values part of the uniqueness scope.
